description: The bar chart displays the average performance across five training methods—labeled 'Standard,' 'Self-RAG,' 'FactTune,' 'ClInGS (w/),' and 'ClInGS'—arranged in ascending order of performance along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis is labeled 'Average Performance' and spans from 0 to 60 in linear increments of 10 units. Each bar corresponds to one method: the 'Standard' method is represented by an orange bar with an approximate value of 54; the 'Self-RAG' method is shown as a beige bar at approximately 55; the 'FactTune' method is depicted by a green bar at approximately 52; the 'ClInGS (w/)' method is represented by a blue bar at approximately 55; and the 'ClInGS' method is shown as a dark blue bar at approximately 62. The bars are not sorted in descending order, and there are no visual emphasis features such as shading, bolding, or annotations on any of the bars.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average performance across five training methods on 11 datasets. The horizontal axis lists the methods: 'Standard,' 'Self-RAG,' 'FactTune,' 'ClInGS (w/),' and 'ClInGS,' in ascending order of performance. The vertical axis represents 'Average Performance,' ranging from 0 to 60, with intervals of 10 units. The 'ClInGS' method consistently outperformed all others, achieving an average performance of approximately 62, while 'FactTune' showed the lowest performance at around 48. The 'Self-RAG' method demonstrated a slight decline compared to 'Standard,' which maintained stable performance across datasets. The chart highlights the superiority of the 'ClInGS' methods, particularly the standalone 'ClInGS' approach, which exhibited a significant improvement over its variant 'ClInGS (w/).'
